name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Oregon dairy-linked case 19 Nov; 4 US since Oct
summary: No new human H5 case found from 20 to 24 Nov; four US dairy-linked cases since mid-Oct, no human-to-human spread
state: Oregon Health Authority confirmed on 19 Nov a human H5 case linked to a Morrow County dairy outbreak and said the virus is not known to spread between people (OHA). ECDC's 3 Nov update recorded three cases in Yakima County, Washington, one fatal, tied to exposure to infected dairy cattle (ECDC). Searches from 20 to 24 Nov found no further human case and no cluster. Cases remain sporadic and animal-linked, so Normal holds.
for_you: The risk to the general public is low. People who work with poultry or dairy cattle should follow official guidance from UKHSA or CDC on protective equipment, and report dead or sick wild birds to the relevant authorities rather than touching them.
rubric_hit: Normal: sporadic animal-to-human cases only; no human cluster or human-to-human spread

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
